utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecution versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Registrar. Today is the 9th of April, 2008. I would like to greet the representatives of the Prosecution, the witness, as well as Mr. Seselj, and all the people assisting us today. This hearing is dedicated to the interview of a witness as part of the 92 ter procedure. Last week, and no later than yesterday, Mr. Seselj told us that he did not wish to cross-examine this witness, but I don't know whether he will cross-examine the witness. After a good night's sleep, sometimes one can change one's mind, whatever the case may be. The proceeding will unfold as follows: The Prosecutor will briefly summarise the written statement of the witness, will put the traditional questions to the witness on the content and the truthfulness of what he has said, and in addition the Prosecutor can also put questions to him and show him a few documents. After that, the Bench will put questions to the witness. I shall therefore ask the witness to take the solemn declaration. I will ask the witness to stand, please. Sir, can you give me your first name, last name, and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Fadil Kopic. I was born on the 5th of March, 1966.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have an occupation currently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unemployed at present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have been on the dole for how many months, how many years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I haven't been working since the end of the war, so for 15 years, roughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have a source of income? Do you have subsidies? Do you have a personal fortune? How do you live? How have you been living for the last 15 years? What do you live off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I receive some social benefits from the municipality. I'm on welfare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I might ask a question before I ask you to take the solemn declaration. You have been interviewed by the OTP, but have you been interviewed by any other investigators or police officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read the text of the solemn declaration now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to the Prosecutor, some information I would like to impart to you, and I would like to explain to you how this hearing is going to unfold. I will, after that, give the floor to Mr. Seselj, who would like to take the floor. You will have to answer questions which the Prosecutor will put to you. You have met him, I'm sure, over the weekend or a few days ago with a view to preparing this hearing. After that, I will put a number of questions to you and my colleagues will put a number of questions to you, and if need be, I will ask Mr. Seselj if he has any intention of putting questions to you. Once all the questions have been put, you can then leave and go back home. Mr. Seselj, I believe you raised your hand and wanted to raise something. What would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, before the witness took the solemn declaration, I wanted to raise an administrative issue. Now, if that's possible now, I'll do it now. If not, I'll do it after the break. It has nothing to do with this witness at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes ago, my associates from Belgrade sent me a photocopy of an article that appeared in the Belgrade "Daily Blitz" with a large circulation. It appeared on the 6th of April, the article, and it continues the propaganda war either by the Registry or the OTP of The Hague Tribunal against me, because here, in over half a page, a lie is being stated that in the Detention Unit I met the Defence counsel of Ramush Haradinaj and that British lawyers from Tony Blair's chambers had a meeting with me, too. Now, I don't have an opportunity of addressing the public and making statements for the press, and I demand that the Registry denies this straight away and to investigate whether the lie came from amongst its ranks or from the offices of the OTP, and the Detention Unit administration knows full well that I never had any meetings either with Ramush Haradinaj's lawyers or any other lawyers, for that matter. And if I happen to say hello to a Serbian lawyer in passing, that would be all. So I think that this is truly unbelievable, and I think it's just the first of a series of attempts to launch false news from The Hague Tribunal by those who don't like my successful defence and wish to slander me in various ways. This has inflicted enormous moral damage to me. I can provide a copy for the OTP and the Registry, for copies for the Trial Chamber, et cetera, and I'd like a copy to be returned to me, but I think you must stand up and protect me. Everything that has to do with this Tribunal and the lies put out by the Tribunal in the media and that I'm not able to answer and respond to them, somebody else has to do that in my name for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall make copies and have it translated, and then we will ask the Registry to provide us with further information. And if the information stemmed from the prison -- we shall also give a copy to the Prosecutor. Very well. And we will keep you posted and tell you what the prison warden has to say about this. Mr. Prosecutor, I shall now give you the floor. MR. DUTERTRE [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we briefly move into private session. I have a short issue to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move into private session for a few moments, Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as you have asked me to do, I now suggest reading the testimony of this witness. Let me begin, and I would like the interpreters to let me know if I'm reading too fast: The witness is a Muslim man who was born in March of 1966 in Caparde in the Kalesija Municipality. He completed vocational school training to become a waiter. He also completed military service in 1985-1986 in Zagreb, Croatia. He is married with children. He was 26 years old and still living in Caparde when the conflict began. On May 5th, 1992, the witness and about 30 other people tried to flee from Cerska to free territory. When they reached the village of Planinci, a part of the group, including the witness, was arrested and detained by civil police officers. The witness and his companions were taken to the Serbian village of Vidovici. There, the witness saw men in civilian, police and military clothes. The detainees were searched and their money, documents, watches and gold were taken. Then they were ordered to lie on the ground and were beaten. One of the captors, an older man with a subara, that is a high fur hat and long beard, said that he would kill them. Another person declared that their orders were to take the detainees to Zvornik. The policemen restrained the witness and the other detainees' hands and loaded them on a truck to Zvornik. The truck first stopped at the Alhos factory in Karakaj, where the police captors spoke to a group of Serb soldiers, with a group of Serb soldiers in green and grey uniform. The soldiers pulled the tarpaulin cover off the truck up to beat them. The witness arrived in Zvornik and the truck stopped at the SUP building, where they were questioned about their background and threatened. After questioning, they were taken back to Karakaj to the Ekonomija farm. At the Ekonomija farm, the witness was placed in a concrete room, 15 to 20 square metres in size, which had blood stains on the wall. There was a window 50 centimetres high with bars on it. For the first few days, the witness had no bedding. Hay and cardboard was eventually provided. There were no soap and no towels. Some guards allowed the detainees to use toilet facilities. They were guarded by men in olive grey JNA uniforms. About two hours after arriving at the Ekonomija farm, a group of soldiers wearing camouflage uniforms came in. They each had pistols and automatic weapon and a knife. They threatened the detainees and cursed them. They cursed President Milosevic and glorified their leader who they said was Vojislav Seselj. Soon the soldiers started beating them. They were kicked and hit with rifle-butts. Some detainees lost consciousness, and water was poured on them to revive them. The witness later learned that these men were from Kraljevo. These men included Major Dragan Toro, Zoks, Pufta, Savo, and Repak. A few days later, the witness was joined by more detainees from the Standard factory in Karakaj. In fact, new detainees often arrived and others left. At one time, there were 40 detainees at Ekonomija. All of the detainees were repeatedly beaten by the group from Kraljevo and a group of five or six military policemen from Loznica, including Rogonja, Brko and Cupo. The witness saw one detainee sexually assaulted. This detainee was then killed. The guards [Realtime transcript read in error "Croats"] did nothing to stop this treatment. Based on what the men from Kraljevo said, the witness believes that they reported directly to Seselj. Pivarski later joined these men and took part in the beatings as well. In one instance, Niski, one of the men from Loznica, lined up detainees and selected the most physically fit. The selected group was then put on a truck and taken to the Novi Izvor brick factory, also known as Ciglana. The witness was not among the selected group. Later that day, the witness was approached by Pivarski and asked if the witness had any money and if he had someone willing to pay for his release. The witness offered 700 Deutsche mark which he had carefully hidden. As a result, the witness was taken to Ciglana. He doesn't know what happened to the others who remained in the detention room at the Ekonomija farm. In Ciglana, the witness worked with the men from Loznica and Kraljevo to loot from empty Muslim houses in the town of Zvornik and neighbouring villages. Trucks transported these items to Serbia. Other detainees worked in Ciglana to make bricks. The beatings resumed in Ciglana. It is the same group that had been beating the witness in Ekonomija, but they did not come as often. The witness remembers one beating where they were told to strip down to the waist. Their bodies were inspected for tattoos. One man had a tattoo on his lower arm. The witness thinks that it showed a crescent moon and star, and a crescent moon. Pufta told him to have the tattoo removed by morning. The man tried to burn it off, but it still showed. Pufta then removed the tattoo with a knife. Pufta also cut the ear of a detainee named Ismet Cirak. Pufta then killed Cirak. While in Ciglana, a group of people was brought in. They said they had been detained at Dom Kulture in Celopek and had been tortured there. In mid-July or late July, the witness was transferred to Batkovic. He stayed there until November 1992 when he was released on a prisoner exchange. [Interpretation] This is the end of the witness's summary. On page 10912, I'm told that there is a translation mistake. I said "guards did nothing to stop this treatment," and in English it says "Croats did nothing." But I said "guards" and not "Croats." If you may, I can now submit the witness's statement according to Rule 92 ter. I gave the usher a small binder with the hearing of this witness. And you can also put this on the screen. This is Exhibit 7190 in the 65 ter list. I would like to have the Serbian version of the document, if possible, so that the witness can look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Kopic, do you remember having been interviewed by an investigator on the July 13 and 14, 1997?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber would like to know exactly what is the difference between a statement and a hearing. In French, "declaration" and "audition." "Interview."

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will check what word I used. It is a written statement, to be extremely specific. Maybe I was using generic terms so that the witness would understand them, but this is a written statement I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Kopic, do you remember having provided a written statement to an investigator from this Tribunal in 1997, on July 13 and 14?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Kopic, you have a binder in front of you, and there's a document also that is displayed on the screen in front of you. I have three questions to ask. The document that you see on the screen and which you have a hard copy of, is this the written statement that you gave to the investigator of this Tribunal on July 13 and 14, 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this written statement faithfully reflect your testimony and what you said to the investigator who put the questions to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to add something, if I may, to what you said. May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: When you were talking about that, that gentleman who was sexually abused at Ekonomija, I don't know what you consider sexual abuse to be, but he was actually impaled. He didn't have contact with another person. And after that, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you for this detail, useful detail.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Ismet Cirak, not Sirak. I don't know how you write these letters, but in our parts you read this as "Cirak."

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. This is quite useful. We'll maybe come back to all this, Mr. Kopic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: May I have a pencil so I can make a note here? I don't want to interrupt you, but I want to be able to go back and correct you if there's a mistake somewhere. Because it might slip my memory if I don't make a note. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Of course. My question, Mr. Kopic: If you were asked the same questions again, would you give the same answers today, if asked the same questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. I'm only talking about what I experienced and what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honour, I would like to tender the written statement, and I would like an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will give a number after we ask the questions ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would now like to display Exhibit 7188 on the 65 ter list. This is a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Kopic, could you, in a very general fashion, tell us exactly what this map represents? What is the area we see on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I see Zvornik, Karakaj, the River Drina here, and the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to tender this exhibit as evidence, to have a blank map available. It might be very useful for the next witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number, please, Ms. Registrar, for this map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P358.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Kopic, in your 92 ter statement, you said that you were arrested in Planinci. Could you please tell us on the map where this is? If you could please place a map -- a cross -- an X on this, and the usher will help us with the pen. Could you please place a cross next to Planinci and circle this cross and number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: This is it. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Please place an A, not "1," "A."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kopic, you also said in your statement that you were detained in Karakaj at the Ekonomija farm. Could you please tell -- show on this map where this Ekonomija farm is located in Karakaj, then place a cross, put a circle around it, and then place a "B" next to this cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I'll do my best, but I can't pinpoint it precisely, since I never looked at this map in this way. It's a bird's-eye view. I think it's somewhere around here, somewhere around here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Very well. Could you do exactly the same thing for the brick factory, Ciglana, where you were then taken, so please place a cross with a circle around it, and a "C" next to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I'll try, I'll do my best. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P359.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like now to have some information on how to continue. Maybe Mr. Kopic can take his headset off for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kopic, could you please take off your headset for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in 1997 the witness drew a sketch of the place where he was detained in Karakaj. I would like some instructions. This number has an exhibit -- this sketch has an exhibit number, and I could display it and so he could recognise it, but maybe we would rather that the witness draws a new sketch. I don't know what you rather -- how to proceed, and I would like your guidance, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, you may use the old sketch. I don't think we need to make a new one. And ask your questions using that sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Kopic can place his headset back on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the witness who drew the sketch?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely, as far as I know. Could I please display Exhibit 2526. Could we zoom out, please. A little bit more. For your information, there is a translation attached to this in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Kopic, could you tell us generally what this sketch represents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, I'm no artist, but this is the Ekonomija area where we spent a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Very well. You drew this sketch, and your signature is on the bottom of the page; is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: On the sketch, we see a number of buildings. Could you tell us in what building you were detained? Can we see it on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: The first building to the right of the entranceway, you can see the door. Do you want me to draw something here?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Your words are enough, because we already have a legend, anyway. Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to tender this exhibit, please. Can we have a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P360.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Now, for the next step, I don't have any sketch that is ready-made, but maybe you could put a blank sheet on the ELMO, because I would like the witness to draw the place where he was detained later on in the Ciglana factory, if the usher could please help him. Mr. Kopic, could you please draw a sketch of the place where you were detained in Ciglana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: May I ... [Marks] The first thing I drew is the Karakaj-Bijeljina road, and then I'll explain as I go along. Around here is the entrance to the Ciglana, the brickworks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you please place an "A" next to the entrance so we remember that it's the entrance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is the room where we were imprisoned [Indicates] and this is the door. Next to the door, there is a window.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you please place a "B" to show the room where you were detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: [Marks]. What I've just drawn was the factory where their products were produced; bricks, roof tiles, I don't know what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please place a "C" there --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: -- to locate the plant. I would like to tender this sketch as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P361.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If we could please keep it for later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, could you please get the drawing back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Usher, could you please make a copy of this drawing for Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just add something? May I? There was some other buildings around there which are not so important. On the right-hand side of the factory, there was a place where we loaded concrete products onto trucks and where they beat us if we were unable to work hard enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this detail, Mr. Kopic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Kopic, let's move on to something else and return to your statement. On page 3 of your written statement in English, you said that you were placed in a room in the Ekonomija farm in Karakaj the day you were arrested, and you say that two hours later, a group of men came in and that they glorified their leader, Vojislav Seselj. Could you give us some details about this and say what words they said when they were talking about Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you the precise day and time, because it was a long, long time ago. It was a few hours after our arrival, and when this group came in, one of the guards outside said, "Here come the soldiers." I don't know whether he called them White Eagles or something similar. When they came in, they started beating us with various objects. They started cursing our president, Alija. They asked us why we had voted for Alija. They said we shouldn't have voted for Milosevic either, but for Seselj. They said Seselj was a wolf. That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How did they describe Mr. Seselj? Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, not "wolf," "god."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: They said he was a god. Well, he was a god to them, not to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Kopic, could you tell us who is the person named Marko Pavlovic ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I can't be very precise. I think he was an important person in Zvornik. I'm not sure, but on one occasion he came to Ekonomija when they were separating off those of us who were more fit for work. I think he was in that group. I'm not 100 per cent sure, but I think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You say "I believe he was there." What made you believe that he was there? Did you see him, did you hear his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I heard one of the guards saying, "Well, Marko will now decide what to do with them," referring to us, the people who were detained with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When the guard said this, how far were you from this guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I can show you that on this sketch. They were passing in front of the building where we were detained. We were in a small room inside. It was only about 20 or 25 square metres in area. And when they were passing by outside, we could hear everything they said. We didn't dare look at them, but you could hear everything. You could hear people breathing. We weren't allowed to make any noise whatsoever, not even to cough, let alone say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How did people react, if you were able to see this, when the guard pronounced the name of Marko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: What people are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: The people who were guarding you, the military who were guarding you. Could you tell me what their reaction was when the name "Marko Pavlovic" what pronounce, if you were able to see this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I said we didn't dare look at anything, we only heard things. But when they came in we would take a look, however, we had to keep our heads down. Otherwise, they would beat us. I didn't know what their reaction was, but I could hear by the sound of their voice that he was some sort of superior to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Another thing now, Mr. Kopic. Who is Meco?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Meco?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you for the pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: He was a gentleman who used to live in Zvornik before the war, and he was with us at Ekonomija for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I don't know what his real name was. "Meco" was his nickname. I can find out and let you know subsequently, if necessary. But I mentioned the name of Petko Hajdukovic. It's somewhere in my statement. Petko Hajdukovic and Meco were both from Zvornik. They used to live there before the war. Petko would often beat Meco when he came in with a big stick or a rifle-butt. He beat him a lot. He would beat him almost until the stick broke. And then one of those soldiers took him away. After the war, I heard he had been killed somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Who told you that he had been killed? How did you get to know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I was with many people who knew him, even with his father-in-law and with friends and neighbours of his, and it was they who told me that Meco had been killed. I don't know how he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: After he had been taken, did you ever see him, as of the moment he was taken until you learned by his father-in-law that he had been killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kopic, who is Muhamed -- I probably don't pronounce the name correctly, so please correct it for me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: As for the name "Muhamed," I'm not sure whether it's "Muhamed" or "Hamo." That was a nickname. That was a lad who was brought to where we were in the Ciglana, that room I sketched. When they brought in a group of people, there were hundreds of people there, a Serb who was a neighbour of his tried to save this young man. He brought him to us, so he stayed with us for a certain time, and later on -- well, first a group was brought from the direction of Sapna, of Bijeljina, towards Karakaj on the left-hand side. Later, when they were going back in these buses, one of the soldiers came to get Muhammad and he got him on the truck, and they drove off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You mentioned the group of people in buses. Could you be a bit more specific? We'll take this one step at a time. Who were the people on the buses that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: That lad who was with us, he said those people from Sapna, Bijeli Potok, Djulici, those villages, there were about 700 of them, and when they were taking these people somewhere in buses, they stopped the buses to get Muhammad in, and we saw them sitting in the buses with their heads down. And all these groups I mentioned, the names that are in my statement, we saw them being beaten and cursed at. This was very close to where we were in that Ciglana, and you could see what was going on up there on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So at the time, could you tell us where exactly you were? On which road were the buses that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, the sketch I made just a minute ago, when we were in Ciglana, you know, we were in a room, and there was a window facing the Karakaj-Bijeljina road. We were inside that room which I sketched.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Very well. And the buses were on the road; is this what you said? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How long did the buses stay on this road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Maybe 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know why they stopped in that exact location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I think they stopped to pick up that lad who was with us, and maybe for some other reasons, but none that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You say "that young man." Do you mean Hamo or this other person we mentioned a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And who was escorting these people on the bus? Were you able to see who it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, there were all sorts of soldiers there, some dressed in camouflage, some in civilian clothes. Among them were those groups that I mentioned in my statements, during the escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When you talk about the groups you mentioned in your statement, could you repeat this, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, I can. These two groups from Serbia, those from Loznica and from Kraljevo. When I'm saying "those from Kraljevo," that's how we referred to them, although they had not introduced themselves to us. Really, only some of them said they had been from Kraljevo. The other ones, since they were called "Nis" people, they must have been from Nis, and they forced us to sing one song, "Fire is blazing above Kraljevo, let's see which Chetnik is missing," and they were mentioning somebody named Igor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you for having specified this. If you were able to see, how did the guards behave vis a vis the people on the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Those people on the bus, the detainees, a couple of people -- a couple of men would get in and beat them. Now, from the distance of 50 metres, I wasn't able to see who exactly was doing that, but mainly those groups from Serbia, Kraljevo, Loznica, and Petko was among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the attitude of those people who were being beaten on the buses? Could you describe this to us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Do you mean the victims?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, what could they do? They kept their heads down. You could barely see. They looked miserable. They looked awful to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: After about 15 to 20 minutes, you said they stayed there for 15 or 20 minutes, in what direction did these buses go after that, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Right. Well, they set off from Karakaj, then turned off towards Bijeljina. However, there are many turnoffs from Bijeljina, so I don't know where they ended up. I was only able to watch them for a hundred metres or so, and then I don't know where they continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Prosecutor [as interpreted], I have a whole series of questions to put to you that are of a different nature. First of all, we will go back in time a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your written statement, you mentioned that before the war, before the conflict erupted, you were a truck driver. According to you, when did the conflict start, exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: In Bosnia, the conflict erupted in the beginning of April, it seems to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when the conflict began at the beginning of April, were you a truck driver then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: No. I'm a driver for all categories of motor vehicles. I used to drive some trips engaged by certain people occasionally. Sometimes I did work as a waiter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the conflict began, you mentioned in your written statement that you went to Kula Grad to join the resistance. This is very ambiguous. Were you incorporated into the Territorial Defence or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: First of all, they put me on the reserve force of the police, when we had a mixed police force between Serbs and Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're making progress, because this is something which was not mentioned in your statement. So you were then incorporated into the mixed police force; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You had a uniform and a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, what I was issued by the police force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who told you to go to Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, many men went there from Kalesija, and I, since I worked Zvornik, I was frequently there. My mother is from Zvornik, and I heard from her what's going on, and I went up there with a couple of other men, but I wouldn't like to mention their names for their own safety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there any fighting in Kula Grad between the Serbian and Croatian warring factions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Kula is populated 100 per cent by Muslims. I have both friends and family there. I don't know what Serbs from Serbia especially were looking for there. So I felt it incumbent upon me, as a member of my ethnic group and a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to go there and help my country and my people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your ethnic group? You are a Muslim, aren't you? In Kula Grad, was there any fighting, was there any shots fired, were there any casualties, people wounded and killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I think so, some people were even killed, because as I told you, Kula had a 100 per cent Muslim population, and when the Chetniks captured that area, those Bosniaks who could do it in time fled. Others were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This means I can now put to you a question on the way in which you were arrested. You were part of a group of 30 people, and you were going to the village of Planinci. This group of people, you were wearing civilian clothes, you were wearing camouflage clothing, were you armed? Please tell us more about this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I was in civilian clothes. I know that for certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were wearing plain clothes. Could you tell us what you were wearing? Did you have a coat? Did you have a wallet on you? What were you wearing on that day, and what did you have on you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I was wearing jeans, running shoes, a jacket. I had no weapons whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were arrested, did those people who arrested you search you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They searched you from head to foot, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, please tell me, then, how is it that a long time afterwards you had 700 Deutsche mark on you which you were able to give Pivarski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I had bank notes hidden in my underwear. They frisked us when they searched us, but they didn't really make us take off our underwear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you had hidden your Deutsche mark in your underpants; is that right? You weren't properly searched, in other words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: That's all I could hide, paper. Everything else, they took away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time you were searched, things were taken off you, I don't know, a watch, a ring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm putting this question to you because, as you had 700 Deutsche mark on you, this does raise a question, and you are giving us an explanation which is worth what it's worth. But you are telling us that you hid these 700 Deutsche mark on you. 700 Deutsche mark is quite a lot of money. Where did this money come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, my family was not totally poor. It was enough to sell a calf [Realtime transcript read in error "car"] to have that amount of money, if you were living in a village. I don't think you should confused by that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, a calf, not a car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The group monitoring you in Planinci, you said there were 12 of them. You said there was people who were wearing civilian clothes and policemen, and as you were part of the reserve unit, you were able to recognise these people. Under whose authority were these people who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Those of us who were arrested were 12, but I wasn't able to count those people who arrested us. At that spot where they stopped us, there were perhaps five or six of them. When we came down to the village, there were many more of them, but they were wearing police uniforms, too. They had a blue uniform, a cap, and on that cap they had a tri-colour emblem, red, blue and white, instead of the five-pointed star the police used to have before on their caps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to you, whose authority were they under? Did they report to the army, the police, the civilian/municipal authorities? Who were these people who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: This man, Cevap, whom I mentioned in my statement, he was in a police uniform. There were others who were in camouflage or military olive green-grey uniform. However, they told us immediately to keep our heads down. They searched us, they felled us to the ground and tied our hands. They were wearing all sorts of uniforms, carrying all sorts of rifles and weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At one point in time, you were taken to the village of Vidovici, and there there were three people whom you recognised: Dusan, Cevap and Cizmo. I apologise for the pronunciation. Who are these three individuals who you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Those two, Cevap and Dusan, they were from that area, from Grbavica, Vidovici. That's all one area. Cevap is perhaps two years older than I am, also works in catering, and Dusan, too. And the older man, who was nicknamed Cizmo, I think his real name was Milorad, he was a farmer. His property was next to my mother's, so I knew them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These people whom you knew and who were there, what were they wearing, military clothes, camouflage uniforms? What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Cevap and the other one, Dusan, they were in military uniform. Others, Cizmo, for instance, only had the military shirt on, the olive green-grey one, and he had a rifle in his hand. I can't tell you exactly which kind of rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you had done your military service together with Dusan, did you talk to him at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: You mean at that moment when we were captured?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: No, we said nothing. He just stood there, carrying his rifle. But you have to remember that it was all 15 years ago. I cannot give you the details anymore. I remember the faces and the most important things. I cannot forget that. In small things, in small details, I can be off the mark here and there. I know that those were the people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statement, you say that you were tied by the policeman, your hands were tied, and then you were taken to Zvornik. The policeman didn't have any handcuffs. Usually a policeman doesn't have a rope to tie up people's hands. How were you tied up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Rope. They got hold of some rope and tied our hands. There were three or four policemen around. I don't know if a single one of them had handcuffs, because they were standing on a road which the Muslims used to go to Tuzla. So maybe for those occasions, they had lengths of rope on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were these civilian or military policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: These were civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who was commanding this group, the policemen, the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I think by the time they took us to Zvornik, before they took us to Zvornik, I think it was the policeman I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are taken to the SUP building. What is the SUP? You mentioned the policemen. I heard about the MUP, but what is the SUP? Maybe it's the same thing. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: It's the same thing. It was also called "police station."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are taken to this building, where you're going to be questioned; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes. First they placed us in some sort of garage that was locked, and then there were stairs from that garage that led upstairs to a room in which they interrogated us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they were questioning you, what kind of questions did they put to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Where we were from, why we were there, why we were Muslims. I think one of them pulled out a gun at one point and said, "Why don't you switch sides and become one of us?" I didn't know what to answer. And then they said, "Let's be off with you, and may God help you," something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seemingly, among the policemen there's someone called Boja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes. He had been a policeman even before the war, and I believe at that time he had a higher position than a simple policeman. He was some sort of commanding officer, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a head of the police station in this building or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: He must have been some sort of officer, possibly a commanding officer. He did have some sort of higher rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After that, you are taken to the Ekonomija farm; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you showed us the layout of the place. You drew this sketch, and this is what I'm interested in. This goes to the heart of the matter. What I've just talked about is only a starter. We are now addressing the heart of the matter. Now, let me sum up. You are a Muslim fighter in Kula. You go off with a group. You are stopped and arrested by some people, policemen, amongst others, who question you, and then you are taken to a detention centre, which is Ekonomija farm. What I'm interested in is this: Who was guarding you when you were there? If need be, what connection was there with the accused? Under whose authority were you detained in this farm? According to you, who was guarding the place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I think those were reserve soldiers, older -- they were not young men, they were 40ish, 50ish. They were wearing military uniforms, olive green-grey. They had rifles and they secured the building when the other groups that I mentioned in my statement were absent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you say part of the reserve unit. You mean the reserve unit of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: A man of 40, 50, was no longer a regular soldier in our parts at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You, yourself, did your military service in the JNA in 1985 and 1986 in Zagreb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are reservists who are guarding the place; is that right? Were these people armed and were they wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, they were in uniform and they had weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since they were guarding the place, you yourself could not move around freely and you couldn't escape. We agree on that, don't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Of course. We were not even free to go to the lavatory until we asked for their approval, and then we would go there and get beaten on the way. We would go one by one to the lavatory and go back in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you were detained there, did you have the feeling -- of course, this goes back some time, this was more than 15 years ago. I know it's difficult to remember, but did you feel that in this location there was a head, there was a commander of some sort, or was it total chaos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: There was somebody who ruled, although there was some chaos as well. I just don't know who it was who ruled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Someone was in charge, could you tell us who this was or didn't you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I don't know who exactly, in particular, was in charge. I know there were those two groups from Serbia. In one group, Major Toro and Pivarski were the men in charge. In the other group, I don't know, they were separate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're getting close to the core issues. He told us that you were beaten -- you were detained, you were beaten up. I'm not going into this in any detail, because it's not the purpose of the questions I'm putting to you. My question is: Who beat you up, who was heading this, who was in charge, who was responsible? Seemingly, there is a group who comes. This is the so-called Kraljevo group. You mentioned a few names, Toro, Zoks, Pufta, Savo and Repak. You mentioned nicknames and names. And this small group of individuals is not the same as the group of people guarding the place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, they did not guard the building. They came to fetch us when they were about to beat us. However, there were other men whose names I don't remember who would sometimes come together with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they came to beat you up. Where did they come from? Were these locals, did they come from Zvornik? Where did they come from? Or perhaps they lived there. Where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question. They would just come through the door. I don't know where they're coming from, from which direction, from which road. We had no contact with the outside world.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They'd come on foot, by bicycle, on horseback, they'd come by car, in a truck? According to you, how did they get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, you could hear the sound of a car when they were coming, when we were in the Ekonomija farm. In the Ciglana, in the brickworks, we could see them in cars through the windows. Cupo would sometimes come on a motorcycle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, did you feel that the sole purpose of their coming was to beat you up, or did they come to check that you had no more money on you, no more gold, no more valuables which they wanted to take off you, or did they only come to beat you up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, while we were at the Ekonomija farm, they only came to beat us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell us how they were equipped? Were they well equipped, ill equipped? What was it like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: They were very well-equipped. They had camouflage uniforms, they had two or three guns -- pistols apiece, they had automatic rifles. They had even truncheons to beat people with. For a while, Toro carried around a baseball bat. Their uniforms were quite nice. Special equipment, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were particularly well-equipped. What were they wearing on their heads, a beret? What did they have on their heads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, as for headgear, I'm not sure everyone wore something on their heads. They were bare-headed most of the time, because it was warm, but sometimes they would wear berets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a crucial question now. Did you see, at any point in time, did you see an insignia on these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of insignia. Rank insignia or a badge? What?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Insignia. I'm not talking about ranks, I'm talking about insignia. I'll show you three. I'd like to ask the Registrar to put page 109, 110 and 111 on the ELMO, please. Please show page 109 first. This is an insignia. Did you see an insignia looking like this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, they did have some signs, but I can't remember now what they were exactly. I can't be precise, but they did have some on their shoulders, on their arms here, up here [indicates]. But not all of them had them, and it was a long time ago, a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We now show you the next page, page 110. This is another insignia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I've already said they had something, but I can't be specific. I can't say what exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Next page, 111. It doesn't ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, I did see -- I saw all these, but I can't say exactly where and when. All this is known to me. I was in the camp in Karakaj, Batkovic and so on, but I can't be specific and say this one had that sign and the other one had the other sign. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I've just shown you three insignias potentially allocated to the White Eagles. In your written statement, you mentioned that they belonged to the White Eagles, that these people belonged to the White Eagles. I've shown you three insignias. Had you seen them either there or elsewhere or are you seeing them for the first time today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: No, I'm not looking at them for the first time today. I did see this insignia, and I heard the White Eagles come to the door. They would comment with the guards, and then the guards would say -- or when there was somebody at the door, they would say, "Well, the White Eagles are coming now."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That's what the guards would say. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll get the document back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am familiar with this. I do know these emblems and I can read what it says on them. But as I say, so much time has gone by, and let me repeat that, I can't say that Zoks had this one and the other one had the other one, but they certainly did have insignia on them of some sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You just said something very important. A guard told you, "The White Eagles are coming now." You remember that? So these individuals who came and who were well equipped, armed, and you told us that some of them had an insignia, you believe that these were the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: The men who came had some insignia, and the guard said that the White Eagles would come. Now, whether they were actually the White Eagles, I can't say, because they didn't introduce themselves and say, "We're the White Eagles." When they beat us, they swore at us and glorified Seselj and that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm gradually reaching the heart of the matter. You said that when these individuals arrived, they allegedly told you, "Why didn't you vote?" They were extremely hostile towards Milosevic, and seemingly, when answering the Prosecutor, you said that they mentioned Mr. Seselj. Let's go back in time. In 1992, when you were a reserve policeman, had you ever heard the name of Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, through the media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. My fellow Judge is telling me that it's time for the break, so we will take a break, and we will resume with the questions after this 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just before the break, I was putting questions to you about Mr. Seselj, and I asked you to go back in time. I asked you whether you had heard about Mr. Seselj, and you said, "Yes." Could you please tell the Bench when you heard the name of Mr. Seselj, and could you tell us who Mr. Seselj was for you, before the conflict started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, I said that I heard the name before the conflict in the media, and then later on in the camp from the groups I mentioned, they glorified him and would say that he would -- that he was God and things like that to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You say "in the media." At the time, did you have a radio, television, did you buy newspapers? How did you obtain your information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, watching television, the news on television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And on the TV news, they were mentioning Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, because in 19 -- well, before the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you had the battlefield in Croatia, so the media would explain what was going on there. And on a couple of occasions, I heard that name mentioned, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The television that you could watch on your TV set, was it the Belgrade Television, Sarajevo Television, or Zagreb Television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Mostly Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In the Ekonomija farm, we have these individuals which are called the White Eagles by one of the guards, and you say that these individuals were glorifying Mr. Seselj, saying that he was a god. If you remember, could you give us some additional information on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to tell you. They glorified that name and beat us, and it was assumed that he was their god and, therefore, their leader. That's how those of us who were incarcerated thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are telling us that because they glorified Mr. Seselj, you assumed that this group may have a connection with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, of course. The only person they glorified was him, so who would be their leader? They didn't glorify any other person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That was the first group. And then there was another group coming from Loznica. Who were these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, I named a few names. They were some sort of reserve, perhaps police force. They were armed nicely, well equipped, and both groups -- well, how shall I put this? People -- they appeared to me to be like people from the street who were full of anger and wanted to express it. They didn't leave the impression of being different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Loznica group, in your written statement you mentioned three people, and I apologise in advance for the pronunciation. Cupo, Brko and Rogonja or something like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Rogonja, he got the nickname before the war. He worked in a cafe in Loznica or near Loznica in Serbia. As for Cupo and Brko, we gave them those nicknames. Cupo had longer hair and Brko had a moustache, so we chose the nicknames accordingly to reflect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. These people who came from Loznica, according to you, were they under the authority of the army, of the civilian police, of the military police, or of some unidentified group? What can you tell us about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, they were all sorts. Some wore reserve military uniforms, other wore police uniforms. Cupo had some sort of camouflage uniform, military, but certain individuals wore police uniforms, you see, depending on how they were equipped, what group they belonged to, who issued them with this equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These two groups would come in to beat you up. I mean, at least the guards had to agree with them. Otherwise, they would not have let them in. What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: On the contrary, I think the guards were just there to prevent us from leaving the premises. But when they turned up, they did whatever they liked, and I don't think the guards could influence them at all. That was my impression, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your written statement, there is a brief episode about the Novi Sad TV, who came to film you. Could you tell us exactly what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: That was while we were at the Ekonomija. They arrived, one with a camera and one of the journalists, and before that, before they came in and activated the cameras and microphones, they told us -- we were told that we were going to be filmed and that we would make statements, but that we were not allowed to say that anybody beat us or behaved badly towards us. And they told us to say that we were some paramilitary units and things like that and that we were fine there. So they prepared us for what we should say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You, yourself, were filmed, and you also made a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, they did film us. I don't know what we said. The filming lasted a few minutes, and later on I heard that they broadcast this over Television Novi Sad and that they said that they had captured the Muslim Green Berets and things along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And did you say a few words on the microphone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I did say something, but I don't remember exactly what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the Green Berets, you did not belong to the Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: No. I think that that formation, the Green Berets, didn't actually exist in the area that I lived in, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have two other questions regarding Niski and Pivarski. I carefully listened to your answers to the Prosecutor. You said that you believed that Niski came from Nis. You recognised his accent, and I was very interested by this. I would like to ask you the following question: In your own region at the time, you were able to recognise where a person came from just by listening to this person's accent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, yes. In the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were a lot of different accents and dialects, and that's the case in Serbia, too. You can differentiate between people's accents. In Sarajevo, for example, although the same language is spoken, the accent is a bit different, and you can distinguish people from various parts of Serbia based on their accent as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This group from Kraljevo, Toro and the others, did they also have an accent that could make it possible to recognise them and to say that they came from Kraljevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, they had the typical Serbian type of accent. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the group from Loznica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I think they had a similar accent. Well, I don't know their accents specifically. I know that in Vojvodina, they tend to draw out their syllables whereas in Nis, for example, in my opinion, they speak a little faster and swallow some of the syllables but they are fairly similar. I don't live there but I go to Serbia from time to time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the written statement, you mention Pivarski at one point in time, and you say that he came from Vukovar. What did you base that on, that he came from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, he told me that personally, that he was from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to you, why did he come from Vukovar to the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, I think that at one point he told me that he and Niski were at the battle front in Vukovar at one time and that then they crossed over into Bosnia. I don't exactly know why, but that was the story he told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. One question before last. In your written statement, you talk about how Pufta killed Cirak. You describe what happened. Through your detention, how many people were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I saw three killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I saw three dead men with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question. At the end of the questions asked by the Prosecutor, you said that later on you were freed during a prisoner exchange. Within this prisoner exchange, were these -- was this an exchange of war prisoners, or were civilians exchanged for civilians, or were civilians exchanged for military soldiers? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I was exchanged on the 24th of November, 1992, in a place called Satorovici. I was in Batkovici, where there were about 1.600 of us, and we were visited by the International Red Cross at one point. And whether they organised the exchange, I don't know. We were in the camp, most of us were civilians there, you know, and on the opposite, too. When the exchange took place, we just went one way and the others went the other, in the opposite way, and they were all dressed in civilian clothes, all of us on both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the war, after 1995, did you register as a veteran in order to be granted a veteran's pension or did you decide not to register?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes, I was registered as a combatant of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were freed on November 24th, 1992. After this, did you join the ABiH? What did you do after you were freed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: First of all, I underwent treatment for several months, and then I went to the army, BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And which corps or which brigade were you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: 3rd Corps, 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I believe my fellow Judges have questions to put to you also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just one question. Except from the fact that you heard the people who were beating you talk about Seselj, were glorifying Seselj, and asked you to vote for Seselj, did you ever hear from either the people who were beating you or by others that they were Seseljevci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Do you mean the people from Kraljevo, that they were Seselj's men, or whether his units existed at all? I don't really understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm asking you whether the people who were beating you up, those from Kraljevo or Loznica, did you ever hear them say -- or did you ever hear others say about them that they were Seselj's men, Seseljevci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Well, that's what they said themselves, and I said that in my statement and a moment ago, that they would swear to Seselj and said that we should vote for him and that they sung his praises and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We must be very specific, we must obtain very specific answers. Maybe it's my fault. I did not ask you whether these people were glorifying Seselj. You said this, this is clear, they glorified Seselj and they said that you were to vote for Seselj. Fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Not that we had to vote, but that we should have voted for him. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute. You, except for the statements here, you only mentioned people who were glorifying Seselj and who allegedly would have told you that you should vote for him. So far, this is all you've told us about Seselj here. Now, I would like to know the following: Regarding these people who were beating you up, have you ever heard either them or others say that they were Seseljevci, which means Seselj's men, that they were Seselj's volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure that they, themselves, said that they were his men, but they did speak about him, said all the best about him, sung his praises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kopic. I also have just a few questions for you, and my questions relate to the distinction between the various groups that came to beat you in the Ekonomija factory. You have told us about the group from Loznica. You have told us about the group from Kraljevo. And you also told us at a certain point of a group of White Eagles. First of all, just to be sure, the group from Kraljevo, were they the White Eagles that you spoke about or are we talking about two different groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: They were two groups, the Loznica and the Kraljevo group, but this lot belonged to the Kraljevo group. At least that's what people said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. So the White Eagles who came to beat you at a certain moment, they were, in your understanding, members of the Kraljevo group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: They were from Kraljevo, that first group that came to beat us. Well, that's how they introduced themselves, that's what they said, which does not mean that there was not somebody that might have been from Belgrade or Nis amongst them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Maybe I'm not expressing myself clearly. I want to find out if the group from Kraljevo is one and the same group as the group that you have referred to as the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. Another question relates to the visits that you had from the ICRC in the Batkovic detention, and my question is: Were you given a chance to talk to the members of the ICRC in private and individually or were you speaking to the ICRC representatives in groups, and were there some of the guards present during the interviews?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: When they came to visit us, the International Red Cross, in front of the hangar there was a tent where there was a bench, where we sat, and they registered us then. And right behind the tent, so through the canvass, were the Serb soldiers who were guards there. So quite possibly they could hear everything we talked about. However, when they were supposed to come and visit us, and the first time they came and in future as well, they would always set aside the minors and the elderly from that camp, Batkovici, and they would take them to some forest to hide them there. So when they would leave, they would bring these people back to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So the ICRC never saw the children and the elderly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I don't think so, because they took the children off and then I think for a time they let them go to Bijeljina, to some relatives or friends. And later on I heard that some of them were transported across Hungary to some other countries, to some third countries, the children who were under age and the more elderly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks. Just to get back to my question relating to the interviews with the ICRC: Were you taken to the tent individually or in groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: One by one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to finish it off, one last question that does not have to do with the facts but rather to procedural matters. After the Washington Agreements in 1995 and the peace, could you tell us in what circumstances you were contacted to testify for the OTP? I would like to know whether you contacted them, yourself, or whether one day your phone rang and an investigator from the OTP called you in order to meet up with you. Could you tell us exactly what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1014
utterances.text: I first gave statements when I came there from the camp, Kalesija and Tuzla, and then later on somebody called me up and said some of the internationals would come, for me to give statements. So it wasn't me, personally, who asked for that, but I didn't decline. I agreed to cooperate when they came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were interviewed by the OTP in these circumstances. Very well. Another question now. At any point in time, were you contacted by the secret services of your own country, who would have prepared you for possible testimonies or future interviews?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I believe that I was right to ask questions. You went to Belgrade. We're going to have to redact this. This is in line with what we said earlier. And I think we should move to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Judges are finished with their questions, and now they turn to Mr. Seselj and they would like to know whether he wishes to cross-examine the witness or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Prosecutor, do you have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No additional questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
