utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. Mr. Kopic, on behalf of my fellow Judges, I'd like to thank you for having come to The Hague to testify, and we wish you the best for your return in your own country. I would now like the usher should escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too. I wish you success in your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have an oral decision that needs to be made. It's a bit lengthy, but we have plenty of time for once. Oral decision on lifting the confidentiality of the transcript of April 1st, 2008. Noting the oral motion made by the accused on April 2nd, 2008, in view of lifting the confidentiality of excerpts of the transcript of April 1st, 2008, noting that the Trial Chamber considers that the confidentiality of the excerpts mentioned hereunder may be lifted because they did not make it possible to identify the protected witness who testified on April 1st and 2nd, 2008, and I will say exactly what pages and lines are involved. Page 5541, lines 6 to 23; page 5542, line 21, to page 5544, line 24; page 5545, lines 14 to 25; page 5546, lines 13 to 24; page 5553, line 14, to page 5554, line 2; page 5554, line 7, to page 5556, line 9; page 5556, line 20, to page 5562, line 17; page 5569, line 14, to page 5571, line 12; page 5571, line 17, to page 5571, line 18; page 5580, line 11, to page 5581, line 4; page 5569, line 12, to page 5590, line 17; and, finally, the last page, 5597, line 20, to page 5598, line 11. This was a bit lengthy, but it had to be done. These pages are the French transcript. We have to say this so there's no errors. I mentioned the pages for the French transcript and not for the English transcript. Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, after the hearing of Witness Kopic, could we please have an exhibit number for the witness statement, according to Rule 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... as you read. Could we please have a number for Mr. Kopic's witness statement?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 362.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move back to private session for a couple of minutes, because the Trial Chamber must issue another decision, and this time confidentially.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session, tomorrow we have a witness who has been scheduled, but for administrative reasons this witness was unable to come today. Had he been here today, we could have started his testimony today, but we cannot, and we will start his testimony tomorrow. Unfortunately, we might not be able to finish his testimony tomorrow because we have planned two hours for the Prosecution, as part of the examination-in-chief, and Mr. Seselj will also have two hours. Since more often than not time is wasted because of procedural issues, it would be quite remarkable if we would be able to finish tomorrow, but we have planned two hours for the Prosecution. If the Prosecution only has an hour, hour and a half, then we might be able to make it. But that would only be if no procedural issues are raised, which are time-wasting. If the Prosecution actually has all of its time and if there is any redirect, the witness will then have to stay on until next week, and I don't see how we could do otherwise. Whatever the case may be, we are quite sure that this witness is coming tomorrow. And as far as the following week is concerned, the week after that, I had rather that the issue of upcoming witnesses be settled at the beginning of the hearing, rather than addressing this at 25 minutes past 6.00 or 20 minutes past 1.00, when it is time to adjourn. Mr. Mundis, are there any issues concerning next week? Will there be any difficulties? What is it to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: As of right now, there are no difficulties, Mr. President. One must always wait and see what transpires over the course of the next few days. But as of right now, there are no anticipated problems with the schedule for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, in light of cells transfer, because there is work underway in the detention centre, have all the issues been settled, in other words, the ones you mentioned to us last time?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problems cannot be settled until these works are over. It will take about three weeks, 21 days, perhaps until the end of this month. I just got two additional cells, and all my documents are placed there in boxes. I'm not going to unpack the boxes at all. It's impossible to unpack them and sort them out, because there are no shelves or anything. So just the boxes are stored there, but I have the documents here for the next two witnesses, for next week and the week after, and unless the witnesses are replaced and changed by other witnesses, then I will have no problem. And then in May, things will be normal when the works are finished. If the witness lists change until May, then I'll have insurmountable problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As of now, the Prosecutor is telling us that there is no changes in store. We'll take due note of this, but we never know. There's always surprises that can come up at any time. But as of now, obviously everything is well underway and well planned. Mr. Mundis, please, could you have this list of video that could be seen, if need be, as a backup? That would be nice. You told us that you would prepare this, and I still don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honours, is it's still being worked on, and as we indicated yesterday, what we're trying to do is narrow the video list down so that the Trial Chamber has only those videos which are absolutely crucial, in terms of the Prosecution's case. I will make some inquiries this afternoon with members of my team who are working on that component, and we will endeavour to provide further information and/or to get the list to the Chamber and the accused as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In my mind, and I believe that it's also in the minds of my fellow Judges, the videos that we see under these conditions may also be, if need be, shown to other witnesses. That's a possibility. But the videos are useful for the following reasons: When you will have explicit reference to these videos in your final submission, with the footnotes, given that these videos will back your case, or another criterion would be that these videos are corroborating what a witness might have said, either in one direction or another, I believe that this is the usefulness of these videos. The Trial Chamber agrees, and I believe that Mr. Seselj also agrees, on the fact that these videos must be the most efficient and the most relevant ones, the ones that will be the most useful to everyone. It's a waste of time to show a video that will not be used in the end. Of course, I would like to reassure Mr. Seselj, because when his time comes, if he has videos to show, the Trial Chamber will watch them exactly under the same conditions as the other ones, notably regarding the issue you mentioned. When we see an excerpt from a video, when we see a clip, sometimes the clip doesn't mean anything if there's no context. You, yourself, noted this kind of problem, so this is why you should maybe give us the contextual elements that will maybe contradict the Prosecution's case, and we can have hearings that will be devoted specifically to listening to and watching videos provided by the Defence. The Trial Chamber is not excluding to see other videos in the future. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The basic problem has not been solved yet, the problem of obtaining video footage. The Registry has not found a solution, and I presented the problem to you a few days ago. When somebody brings from outside DVDs, then they have to turn them over to the prison authorities to be examined, and then I get them after a while. Why would I allow anybody to see them before I do? I don't want to do that? I am the one who decides whether a video clip will be shown in the courtroom or not. Why would the prison authorities look at it and then possibly make copies, or maybe the Registry would do that and God knows who, and then only it reaches me and then only I can select what to use in the courtroom or not. I must have privileged rights over those video recordings. They have to be brought to me, given me to take in my hands, and only then it makes sense. I'm not afraid for the contents. I just insist on the principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This question did not escape me. A few months back, I had mentioned it and I had talked with the Registry about it. So far, the Chamber did not decide anything. Maybe -- let me state the problem once again. The accused is self-representing himself, and when either Prosecution witnesses come or when Defence witnesses come, he may want videos to be shown, and to this end the accused has told us on several occasions that he had to see the footage himself, beforehand, in order to know exactly how to use them. Insofar that Mr. Seselj said on different occasions that he was in charge of his own defence and that his associates are only here to carry out his instructions. And then Mr. Seselj asked us to make sure that prison management allow him to have access to DVDs, without any prior control by the administration, and here maybe I'm interpreting Mr. Seselj's mind, but he believes that if there is control, there would be interference as far as the rights of the Defence are concerned. Now, this being said, the position of the Registry and of the detention centre is as follows, and I will sum it up: According to the Statute and the Rules, they have the responsibility to make sure that everything is running smoothly in the jail, and because of this, they must control everything coming in the jail, except, of course, for the control of a lawyer-to-client relation. Apart from that, they are entitled to control everything coming in the jail. As an example, let's imagine that an accused wants to see a cartoon, for example. Well, inasmuch as it would be the right of the Defence, this cartoon video would not be submitted to a prior control, and this could be a problem for the -- for prison management. This is how things stand now, but as we see, this is quite difficult and complex. As of now, the Trial Chamber made no decision on this. We're still thinking about a procedure that would help arrange the accused and prison management, but I must say that we have not found any solution yet. But we are fully aware of the problem. Unfortunately, we don't have a solution yet. The Trial Chamber may have to issue a written decision on this, which may be -- may lead to an appeal, and maybe the Appeals Chamber will find a solution in its great wisdom. It seems that the Appeals Chamber finds a solution regarding other problems. But it is now time to adjourn. Thank you all, and we will meet again tomorrow at 8.30. I would like my fellow Judges to confirm this. Yes, obviously they confirm this, so we will meet again tomorrow at 8.30.
